nodes.text: Monomer F is expressed as an immature F0 precursor in infected cells and is subsequently cleaved by host proteases such as TMPRSS234 to generate an F1–F2 heterodimer linked by two disulfide bonds, which in turn forms the mature homotrimer prefusion structure (figure). Globular prefusion F protein is metastable and undergoes an extensive conformational change upon activation. During the fusion process, the F1 N-terminal hydrophobic fusion peptide (FP) of F inserts itself into the target cell membrane, with two spatially separated heptad repeats (HRA and HRB) refolding into a long trimeric coiled-coil helix bundle. This refolding brings the virus and host membranes together and creates a fusion pore through the connected membranes forming the so-called rod-like stable postfusion conformation of F (figure).35 The fusion process is triggered upon binding of F to the host receptor and low-pH stimulation in a few hMPV A genotypes.29,36 Arg-Gly-Asp (RGD)-binding integrins, heparan sulfate (HS), and DC-SIGN and L-SIGN proteins are recognised as viral binding receptors.37–39 hMPV F has a well conserved RGD-motif and blocking integrin binding can restrict viral infection.37HS is another potential F-binding receptor that mediates viral infection independent of integrin.38DC-SIGN and L-SIGN act as entry receptors that bind to the mannose glycan ligand; however, the specific viral protein remains unknown.39 Nonetheless, direct interactions between these receptors with viral target proteins and the exact binding sites of each receptor require validation. current development of hMPV-protective MAbs is focused on MAbs that target the viral F antigen and not the entry receptor. focus F-specific nMAbs.
